# Post-mortem on the Website Registration Conversion Drop

- Date: 2026-10-28 (Wednesday)
- Duration: 02:00
- Participants: 林舟, 陈默, 苏晴, 周远

## Summary
The team reviewed the decline in website registration conversion from 12% to 8.5% and attributed it to the late-September registration page redesign, slow SMS verification code delivery, and the addition of lower-converting new channels, then agreed on owners and deadlines for fixes.

## Discussion
### 1. Funnel data and where the drop occurs
- The first step, opening the registration page, was essentially unchanged; the problem is at the second step, where drop-off between completing the phone number and submitting rose from 18% to 35% ([00:11])
- The second step corresponds to the late-September redesign ([00:25])
- Mobile decline is twice that of desktop, consistent with the reported mobile-specific issues ([00:37])

### 2. Registration page redesign
- The new version requires email first and then phone verification, adding a mandatory field, and the email input box is easily covered by the keyboard on mobile ([00:25])

### 3. SMS verification delay
- Logs show SMS verification codes took an average of 40 seconds this month versus 8 seconds previously; the primary channel is being expanded and the backup channel has never been switched over ([00:44])
- Half of users who did not receive the code within 30 seconds closed the page outright ([00:56])

### 4. Channel mix and competitor activity
- Two new channels were introduced this month; they account for 40% of traffic but convert at roughly half the rate of the old channels, pulling overall conversion down by about one point ([01:03], [01:08])
- A competitor promotion is suspected as an additional factor, but no data is available ([01:16])

## Decisions
- Make the email field optional on the registration page and go live before next Wednesday (Nov 4); Su Qing and Zhou Yuan own this ([01:23])
- Add automatic failover to a backup SMS channel, to be completed by Zhou Yuan before this Friday (Oct 30) ([01:23])
- Chen Mo to build a dashboard splitting new and old channel conversion and deliver it to the advertising team before the end of the month (Oct 31) ([01:23])
- On the competitor promotion, first confirm with the marketing team whether one exists, then decide whether to respond ([01:23])

## Action Items
| Item | Owner | Due | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Make the email field optional on the registration page and launch the change | Su Qing, Zhou Yuan | Nov 4 | [01:23] |
| Implement automatic switching to a backup SMS channel | Zhou Yuan | Oct 30 | [01:23] |
| Build a dashboard comparing new and old channel conversion and deliver it to the advertising team | Chen Mo | end of month (Oct 31) | [01:23] |
| Confirm with marketing whether a competitor promotion is running, then decide whether to respond | Not specified | Not specified | [01:23] |
| Produce a first draft of the registration page revision plan for the team to review | Su Qing | Oct 29 | [01:55] |

## Open Questions & Risks
- Whether the suspected competitor promotion actually exists is unconfirmed and unsupported by data ([01:16])
- New channels contribute 40% of traffic at roughly half the conversion rate of old channels, continuing to weigh on overall conversion ([01:08])
- SMS verification latency may persist while the primary channel is being expanded and the backup channel is not yet in use ([00:44])
